 Updates as the Proteas host Australia in Gqeberha
 Play starts after rain forces early lunch
 Any thoughts? Get in touch with Jim on email 
 LIVE  Updated  9m ago James Wallace (now) and Geoff Lemon (earlier) Thu 22 Oct 2026 08.40 EDT First published on Thu 22 Oct 2026 03.00 EDT Share Key events 9m ago Tea - Australia 253-6 (trail by 73 runs)

 1h ago WICKET! Head b Mulder 121, Australia 209-5

 3h ago Play gets under way

 6h ago Preamble 
 Kagiso Rabada and South Africa celebrate after dismissing Steven Smith on day five of the second Test. Photograph: Marco Longari/AFP/Getty Images View image in fullscreen Kagiso Rabada and South Africa celebrate after dismissing Steven Smith on day five of the second Test. Photograph: Marco Longari/AFP/Getty Images James Wallace (now) and Geoff Lemon (earlier) Thu 22 Oct 2026 08.40 EDT First published on Thu 22 Oct 2026 03.00 EDT Share Key events 9m ago Tea - Australia 253-6 (trail by 73 runs) 
 49m ago BIG WICKET! Steven Smith c Breetzke b Rabada 3 (Australia 225-6) 
 1h ago WICKET! Head b Mulder 121, Australia 209-5 
 2h ago Century! Travis Head 102 from 151 balls 
 3h ago Play gets under way 
 3h ago Lunch taken early 
 4h ago Rain intensifying on final morning 
 6h ago Preamble 
 9m ago 08.39 EDT Tea - Australia 253-6 (trail by 73 runs)
 Simon Harmer beats Alex Carey with a doozy that draws the batter in and then spits past the forward defence. Carey then lap sweeps with aplomb for four and a solid forward defensive sees out the session.
 38 overs bowled, 98 runs added but two crucial wickets lost in the form of Travis Head and Steve Smith. Scott Boland is still there, unbeaten on his highest Test score of 40 and having soaked up a priceless 154 deliveries. Australia’s hopes hang on him, Carey and the rest of the bowlers. There are a potential 45 overs more to survive but bad light could come into it before then. An hour and a half more of resistance could see Australia save the Test. South Africa are desperate for the four wickets needed to level the series and take it to a decider in Cape Town.
 Decent game eh? See you back here in ten.
 92nd over: Australia 253-6 (Boland 40, Carey 12) 
 Share Updated at  08.40 EDT 15m ago 08.33 EDT 91st over: Australia 249-6 (Boland 40, Carey 8) The camera pans to Jason Gillespie in the crowd, just in case Aussie fans wanted a bit more nightwatchman inspiration as Boland gets through another Jansen over.
 Share 20m ago 08.29 EDT 90th over: Australia 248-6 (Boland 40, Carey 7) Alex Carey is a lucky lad! He goes back to a quicker ball from Harmer and almost chops onto his own stumps, fortunately for him and Australia the meaty inside edge bounces over the pegs. Tension ramping up with each over, we’re going down to the final session folks, and potentially down to the wire too.
 Share 22m ago 08.27 EDT 89th over: Australia 245-6 (Boland 38, Carey 6) I do enjoy Jansen’s bowling face, he gives a real surly teenager freshly scolded for having a messy bedroom vibe at the top of his mark. He nearly gets the breakthrough with a beauty to Boland that zips past the defensive prod. So close, so far.
 Share 28m ago 08.21 EDT 88th over: Australia 244-6 (Boland 38, Carey 5) Harmer mixes up his pace, tossing up a flighted delivery and then following up with a couple of darts in an attempt to catch Boland out. He’s got his eye well in by now though and defends robustly.
 Share 30m ago 08.19 EDT 87th over: Australia 243-6 (Boland 38, Carey 4) Eeesht! Boland has started to play a bit more loosely since Smith’s departure, the odd play and miss and unconvincing waft. Its imperative for the Aussies that these two make it through to tea and beyond. A dicey upper cut from Boland to a Rabada short ball lands safely over the infield but there were green and gold hearts in mouths for a split second or two. Head down Scotty!
 Share 32m ago 08.16 EDT 86th over: Australia 240-6 (Boland 36, Carey 3) Harmer whirls away. “Bowling Red” comes the call from Rickelton behind the stumps. Four men around the bat waiting for an edge onto pad to loop up and be swallowed. Boland blocks out five balls after a Carey single off the first. Can’t take your eyes off it.
 Share 36m ago 08.12 EDT 85th over: Australia 239-6 (Boland 36, Carey 2) Just a leg bye and a Rabada front foot no ball off the over. Bavuma calls for Simon Harmer for the next over and the fielders are clamouring to get round the bat. Twenty minutes til the tea interval. Don’t go anywhere.
 Share Updated at  08.13 EDT 38m ago 08.10 EDT 84th over: Australia 237-6 (Boland 36, Carey 2) Boland keeps at it, a 37 year old Duracell Bunny of a man. He gets a meaty edge to Jansen that goes for a streaky four and chastises himself for the loose stroke. A few balls later Marco puts it in the same place and Boland cuts for four with much more composure. The deficit stands at 89 runs.
 Share 43m ago 08.06 EDT 83rd over: Australia 229-6 (Boland 28, Carey 2) Temba Bavuma couldn’t watch the Smith/Breetzke catch as it plooped up, he turned away to look at the crowd like a nervous parent or stressed to all heck football manager during a penalty shootout. He saved himself a palpitation or two not having to witness the juggle from the fielder.
 Alex Carey arrives to join Boland. This pair need to take another hour or so at least out of the final afternoon to give Australia a realistic chance of saving this game. South Africa are hunting the win that will take us to a mouthwatering series shootout in Capetown.
 Carey is off the mark with a single to cover, Boland carries on his brilliant resistance with another textbook push for three through the off side.
 Share Updated at  08.10 EDT 49m ago 07.59 EDT BIG WICKET! Steven Smith c Breetzke b Rabada 3 (Australia 225-6)
 That could well be the game! Smith plays a terrible cross batted hack to Rabada and spoons a catch to Breetzke who juggles the catch as it comes over his shoulder but he takes it at the second grab! What was Smith thinking?! He trudges off and Australia’s hopes now lie with Alex Carey and the bowlers.
 View image in fullscreen Matthew Breetzke makes hard work of the catch! Photograph: Themba Hadebe/AP Share Updated at  08.12 EDT 52m ago 07.57 EDT 82nd over: Australia 225-5 (Boland 25, Smith 3) Jansen shares the new nut. Smith clips the first ball of the over into the leg side for a single, Boland has batted so well that there is no question of shielding strike. Five dots follow but Jansen does beat Scotty B with a beauty that angles in and shapes away late.
 Share 54m ago 07.55 EDT James Wallace 81st over: Australia 224-5 (Boland 25, Smith 2) “The new ball is yours” Geoff says in his handover text. I think that might be the first time in my life someone has said that to me. What a moment. Goosebumps.
 Anyway , what a thrill to be here on the OBO tools for the denouement of this enthralling Test. Rabada has the new ball and Scott Boland now has his highest Test score with a compact push down the ground for four! Some knock this has been, 116 balls faced for his 25 runs and plenty of crucial minutes soaked up. Smith quietly getting his head down with a crook neck, he glides a single past point.
 Share 1h ago 07.45 EDT Geoff Lemon 80th over: Australia 219-5 (Boland 21, Smith 1) Last over before the new Kooka will be Harmer. It won’t be Boland’s eighth maiden of the innings, because he drives Harmer square for two, and equals his own Test high score! Whatever happens after the new ball comes, this has been an admirable effort from a true competitor.
 New ball, new commentator. It’s time for me to go, and for James Wallace to accompany you through Scotty B’s next hundred deliveries.
 Share 1h ago 07.41 EDT 79th over: Australia 217-5 (Boland 19, Smith 1) Mulder got Smith in the first dig, and he’s looking for him again. On the off stump, searching for a way through, but Smith full-blades him to mid on. No run from the over.
 The weather, writes Gervase Greene, “leads me inevitably to the utterly cricket topic of what type of draw might this become? We all know ‘a win is a win’ - be it in football, athletics, darts, life, whatever. But in the age of sudden-death finals, golden points, penalty shoot-outs etc, Test cricket stands supreme for the baffling grey-ness of a draw. There are honorable draws, fortuitous draws, gutsy draws and the downright shabby (ie ‘you should have declined to accept’) draws. I hope the weather improves and this becomes just idle speculation, but I might suggest from an Australian perspective this one lands closer to the latter.”
 This email, admittedly, came through a little while ago, but if Australia do survive today it will be highly creditable. The odds are still with South Africa. Smith hasn’t been himself, Carey is in poor nick, then you get through to the bowlers, Boland’s exceptional defence notwithstanding.
 Share 1h ago 07.38 EDT 78th over: Australia 217-5 (Boland 19, Smith 1) Boland has gone past 100 balls faced. He’s facing Harmer again, still with four catchers, though they’ve swapped one of the off-side men to leg slip, the classic star formation. Finally Boland gets another run, through square, and Smith gets a couple of leg byes in a similar direction. Harmer bowling way too much on the pads. Smith finally gets his first run, flicked square.
 The deficit is 109.
 Share 1h ago 07.34 EDT 77th over: Australia 213-5 (Boland 18, Smith 0) Catch down? Kinda sorta. Smith goes get some bat on Mulder’s ball, but with the keeper standing up to the stumps, that hits Rickelton more than being dropped by him. Defensive shot on off stump from Smith, otherwise it was hitting his woodwork, but the outside edge followed.
 Boland has been on 18 for 10 overs. Smith hasn’t scored. There are 58 overs remaining, and three until the new ball.
 Share 1h ago 07.32 EDT 76th over: Australia 213-5 (Boland 18, Smith 0) Boland’s seventh maiden over faced, seeing off Harmer, but the close fielders are getting interested as the odd one turns.
 Share 1h ago 07.26 EDT 75th over: Australia 213-5 (Boland 18, Smith 0) So Head drives a lovely straight four from Mulder, then gets out. Boland survives him, incongruously. Also incongruous is Steve Smith batting at No7 for the first time since 2014. Guess where that happened? Gqeberha. He gets a bumper from Mulder first up, and it goes through the keeper for four byes.
 Share 1h ago 07.24 EDT WICKET! Head b Mulder 121, Australia 209-5
 The man least likely! He’s the understated name in the seam bowling line-up, but Wiaan Mulder has got the biggest wicket! Head chops on again, again, again, even in this innings, even after a ton. Mulder around the wicket, short of a length, angled in, and Head doesn’t need to play this ball, could have dropped his gloves under it, could have let it hit him, anything. Instead, while hopping, he pushes those gloves at the line of the ball, and deflects it down into his stumps.
 South Africa don’t need to wait for the new ball. They’re in.
 Share 2h ago 07.18 EDT 74th over: Australia 205-4 (Head 116, Boland 18) The lesser-spotted defensive Head carries on being spotted, waiting out Harmer’s over before taking a single from the last.
 That is drinks . Australia now with 61 overs left in the day, and 121 runs to make up. South Africa must remain patient and give themselves the chance of a wicket. Everything can change when one falls, and surely at some stage it will.
 Share Updated at  07.29 EDT 2h ago 07.16 EDT 73rd over: Australia 204-4 (Head 116, Boland 18) Head started the day aggressively but has become very quiet in the last few overs. Into a defensive groove. Mulder the bowler, right-arm seam around the wicket to the lefty, who eventually gets a run to fine leg. He’s not blocking bad balls. Boland defends crisply. He’s approaching his Cowan Ton.
 Share Updated at  07.30 EDT 2h ago 07.11 EDT 72nd over: Australia 203-4 (Head 115, Boland 18) Turn from Harmer, but slow turn from the surface. It starts wide and goes wider, and Head can knock it away easily enough. Cuts the next ball for one run to deep cover. Harmer goes up for a bat-pad appeal against Boland, but that ball was all knee-roll, no bat, hitting outside the leg stump. Harmer’s bowling around the wicket to the righty.
 Boland in Test cricket, by the by, has now opened, batted three, and batted five, six, ten, and eleven. Only number four has eluded him in the top six.
 Share 2h ago 07.07 EDT 71st over: Australia 202-4 (Head 114, Boland 18) Second maiden in a row, as Boland blocks out Mulder. Australia remain 124 runs behind in their second innings. New ball nine overs away.
 Share 2h ago 07.06 EDT 70th over: Australia 202-4 (Head 114, Boland 18) Harmer has swapped ends to the one that Rabada was using. A well set field stops Head scoring while playing the ball into the off side. He’s still there at the end of the over though.
 Share Updated at  07.28 EDT 2h ago 07.00 EDT 69th over: Australia 202-4 (Head 114, Boland 18) South Africa will be starting to grind their teeth. That’s 15 overs bowled this morning and still no wicket. Boland is now playing the longest innings of his career to date, 84 balls and counting. Mulder on, almost bowls Boland while leaving, but it doesn’t nip enough.
 Share 2h ago 06.57 EDT 68th over: Australia 201-4 (Head 113, Boland 18) He is up and away! Looks all set to block a sixth maiden over, then from the last ball decides to uppercut Rabada for four instead. Whoosh. Takes the team past 200.
 Share 2h ago 06.50 EDT 67th over: Australia 197-4 (Head 113, Boland 14) For Head, Harmer has a slip, shot leg, and that short mid off, about 20 paces from the bat. A misfield at cover lets Head off strike. Australia 130 behind. Harmer spears down leg to Boland, in between targeting the front pad, and Boland is able to jab one of those leg-stump balls away for a run.
 View image in fullscreen Travis Head plays a shot. Photograph: Themba Hadebe/AP Share Updated at  07.21 EDT 2h ago 06.47 EDT 66th over: Australia 195-4 (Head 112, Boland 13) Looking confident is Boland. Plays a cut shot and an off drive to Rabada, both to the field, but neatly done. Then fiddles at a line tight to the off stump! Nearly nicks it. Defends the next one well off the back foot, ball angled at his body, and calls “No!” stoutly.
 That’s the fifth maiden he’s blocked out. Faced 70 balls so far.
 Share 2h ago 06.43 EDT 65th over: Australia 195-4 (Head 112, Boland 13) Bavuma is riiiiight under the nose on the off side, almost touching the cut strip with his fingers. I think the umpire might even have moved him back a touch the next ball. He’s close enough to get hit by the bat if Boland steps to the off side to drive. But it’s not Boland who is nearly caught by someone close in, it’s Head after gaining strike. Digs out Harmer to a short straight mid on, full ball, and it just bounces in front of the fielder, who doesn’t claim it but the umpires do choose a quick video check.
